# Final Touches — Murim Login

## Goal

Prepare one mastered chapter for readers. This pass adds footnotes, repairs formatting, and fixes duplicate or missing sentences. It is not a fluency rewrite.

Keep the mastered prose. Change a sentence only to attach a footnote, repair System / thought / speech / chat formatting, restore a source sentence the English dropped, or remove an English sentence the Korean does not support.

## Duplicates and omissions

Compare the English with the Korean source.

- Restore source facts, events, dialogue, and sentences the English dropped, in the same place in the scene.
- Remove English sentences that have no support in the Korean.
- Keep a bold label that names a quoted document, manual, warning, or sign, such as `> **Warning**`. Keep it when this chapter recalls or reprints a notice that was labeled earlier, even if the Korean reprint shows only the body.
- Keep repetition the Korean itself repeats: comedy, panic, emphasis, echoed dialogue, and short beats such as `……`.
- Do not treat a short refrain or a deliberate echo as a duplicate.

## Footnotes

Use Markdown footnotes (`[^1]`, `[^2]`, …). Number them in order of first appearance, starting at 1 for this chapter. Put every definition in one block at the end of the file.

Within this chapter, write one definition for a term, unit, amount, or reference. Every later occurrence of that same thing reuses the same marker. `goshiwon` five times is one note, and so is `hyung`. A different amount or a different term gets its own note. Another chapter may carry its own note for the same term.

Write notes in factual English. No spoilers and no jokes added by the note. Romanize words. A note may include the original character when it is explaining that character. Keep Hangul jamo already used as chat reactions, such as ㅋㅋ and ㄷㄷ.

Add a note only when an English reader would otherwise miss the meaning or the conversion. Skip it when the sentence already says what the reference means. A translated proverb whose warning is plain, a joke the next line completes, a place name used as a place, and a fictional law the dialogue already describes do not get notes.

Skip a conversion footnote when the prose already states both metric and imperial for that quantity.

### Won

Footnote Korean won, including round figures and vague amounts (“hundreds of millions of won”), when the prose does not already give the conversion. Use only the project rates in the packet. Show dollars, then euros, as approximate figures. Round large amounts to about two significant figures and say “about.” For a vague amount, give the approximate range those words cover. One note per distinct amount; reuse it for every later mention of that same amount.

Do not convert traditional money (nyang, taels, cash) or Chinese yuan with the won rate. Explain those with a cultural or historical note only when the English does not already carry the meaning.

### Units

Footnote a Korean or Chinese traditional unit, or a metric quantity, once in the chapter, with both metric and imperial, using this table:

| Unit | Use | Metric | Imperial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pyeong (평) | area | 3.31 m² | 35.6 ft² |
| geun (근) | Korean weight | 600 g | 1.32 lb |
| ja / cheok (자) | length | 30.3 cm | 11.9 in |
| chi (치) | length | 3.03 cm | 1.19 in |
| don (돈) | weight | 3.75 g | 0.132 oz |
| gwan (관) | weight | 3.75 kg | 8.27 lb |
| ri (리), Korea | distance | 393 m | 0.244 mi |
| li (里), China | distance | 500 m | 0.311 mi |
| jin (斤), modern Chinese | weight | 500 g | 1.10 lb |
| liang (两), modern Chinese | weight | 50 g | 1.76 oz |

Choose Korean ri or Chinese li from the setting. Say which one the note uses.

Also footnote metric quantities already in the English (kilometers, meters, centimeters, kilograms, grams, liters, square meters, degrees Celsius) with the imperial equivalent. Use unit words or abbreviations (`ft`, `in`, `mi`, `lb`, `oz`, `gal`). Do not use `"` or `'` as unit marks.

### Cultural references

Footnote a Korean, Chinese, or other Asian word, custom, institution, food, joke, or allusion when the English does not already carry it: `goshiwon`, `hyung`, `doenjang`, `jeonse`. Explain it in one or two sentences. One note per term in the chapter, reused by every later occurrence.

Leave it unnoted when the English is already clear. Do not explain a proverb the translation has already stated, a pun the scene completes, or ordinary vocabulary.

Do not footnote standing series vocabulary. Never add a note whose job is to define any of these, including ordinary variants and compounds:

- Murim
- qi, including demonic qi, innate qi, and qi deviation
- dantian, including the Upper, Middle, and Lower Dantian
- internal energy
- mana

A note about something else may mention these words. Do not attach a marker to them.

## Formatting

Enforce these four patterns. Repair System, speech, thought, and chat formatting when it drifts. Leave every other blockquote heading as it stands.

- **System.** Each real game System panel is one Markdown blockquote headed exactly `> **System**`. Keep the panel’s lines inside that blockquote. Start a new panel only when prose intervenes. Do not wrap System text in square brackets or label a manual, sign, or ordinary quotation as System. A manual or remembered notice keeps its own label, such as `> **Warning**` or `> **Product User Manual**`. That label is not a System panel, and it is not drift.
- **Speech.** Spoken dialogue uses curly double quotes (`“` `”`). Not straight quotes, not italics.
- **Thoughts.** Direct thoughts are italics with no quotation marks.
- **Chat and comments.** Public comment threads and private chat logs shown as threads are one blockquote. Each message line begins with `└`, as in `> └ **Name:** message`. Keep a thread title that is not itself a message, such as `> **Peace Guild**`, on its own line above the messages. Do not add a `**Chat**` heading. A status line that is only a name or level, such as `> **Lv. 22 Hyuk Mujin**`, is not a chat message. Leave that line unchanged, including the bold. Ordinary spoken dialogue stays in curly quotes.
- **Headings.** The only Markdown heading is `# Chapter N`. Do not add `##` or `###`. A diary title or similar label stays a bold line, `**Training Day 1**`, even when the mastered copy used a smaller heading.

Leave narration as narration. Scene breaks stay `* * *`, with the same count as the source.

## Output contract

Return only the complete English Markdown chapter. The first nonblank line must be `# Chapter N`. No status line and no model preamble. Do not add Hangul syllables. Chat jamo and a character cited in a note may stay.

## Project conversion rates

These rates are binding. Do not look up or substitute a market rate.

- 1 US dollar = 1400 Korean won
- 1 euro = 1550 Korean won

Convert every won amount with these rates. In each footnote, give dollars first and euros second.

```text
＃195화



원단 첫날 열린 연회는 대성공이라는 말로도 부족했다.

진위경은 항산검문을 포용함으로써 수십 개 중소 문파의 충성을 받아 내는 파격적인 행보를 보여 줬고, 종남파의 개입과 이미 죽은 줄만 알았던 화왕 적천강의 등장은 모두를 충격에 빠트렸다.

그리고…….

‘그중에는 나도 있지.’

먹고, 마시고, 걸음을 옮기고. 내 일거수일투족마다 사람들의 시선이 따라붙는다.

반나절 전만 하더라도 그 시선들이 뜻하는 것은 ‘산서잠룡’에 대한 관심이었지만 이제는 아니었다.

‘화왕의 제자. 열화문의 계승자.’

곳곳에서 그런 말들이 흘러나오고 있었다. 열화문의 당대 문주인 적천강이 내게 문파의 신물을 넘긴 의미에 대해서, 종남파를 적대하면서까지 태원진가를 보호한 이유에 대해서 쉴 새 없이 떠들고 있다.

‘이거 어째 반쯤 사실로 굳혀진 것 같은데.’

사실 나도 적천강의 의중을 잘 모르겠다. 그래서 이 자리에 있는 거고.

사람들이 정신없는 틈을 타 슬쩍 빠져나온 지금이 바로 적기다.

“후우.”

크게 심호흡했다.

지금 내가 서 있는 곳은 적천강이 머물게 된 처소 앞이었다. 커다란 전각 근처에는 따로 명령이 내려졌는지 쥐 새끼 한 마리 얼씬거리지 않았다.

“적 대협. 계십니까?”

문 너머로 대답이 들려왔다.

“잔다.”

“여쭤볼 게 있어서 왔습니다.”

“잔다고.”

“……주무시는데 대답은 어떻게 하세요?”

“몽유병이니라.”

이게 말이여, 망아지여.

어이가 없었지만 화왕이 그렇다면 그런 거다. 나는 멘탈을 수습하고 다시 입을 열었다.

“저기, 아무리 생각해도 궁금한 게 있어서 말입니다.”

“노부가 네 녀석 궁금증 해결해 주는 사람이냐?”

“그건 아닌데요.”

“잘 알고 있으면 가서 발 닦고 잠이나 자거라.”

철벽 보소. 하지만 여기서 물러설 수는 없다.

굳게 닫힌 문을 향해 아주 조심스럽게, 살금살금 다가가던 그때였다.

“한 걸음만 더 내디디면 내일 뜨는 해를 못 볼 줄 알아라.”

“……어떻게 아셨어요?”

“네놈 인기척이나 천둥소리나 노부에게는 매한가지니까.”

“그러지 마시고 이제 들여보내 주시면 안 됩니까? 아직 겨울이라 날씨도 쌀쌀한데.”

“화염신장으로 뜨끈하게 덥혀 주랴?”

“…….”

거, 듣는 것만으로도 오장육부가 뜨끈해지네.

내가 입을 다물자 침묵이 흘렀다. 한동안 이어지던 고요를 깨트린 것은 적천강의 한마디였다.

“정양(定襄)에 다녀왔다.”

“아.”

보잘것없는 구슬 하나에도 누군가에게는 남다른 의미가 있는 법. 정양이 바로 그렇다.

산서성에 존재하는 수십 개 현읍 중 하나에 불과한 정양의 어느 산길에, 적천강은 가야 할 이유가 있었다.

‘조필.’

하늘이 눈을 펑펑 쏟아 내던 그날, 장천으로 살던 한 사내가 조필이라는 이름으로 죽었다.

“네게 들은 그 자리에서 한참을 머물렀다. 웬 노인이 산기슭을 서성거리니 지나가던 이들이 묻더구나. 왜 여기 있느냐고.”

가라앉은 목소리가 이어졌다.

“바로 이곳에서 피붙이가 죽었다고 대답했다. 남은 시신이라도 수습해 주고 싶어서 왔노라고.”

“…….”

“그때 깨달았다. 너보다 앞서 그 아이를 만났더라도 결코 죽이지 못했을 거라는 것을. 다시 놓아주고 후회했으리라는 것을 말이다.”

문 너머 적천강이 어떤 표정을 짓고 있을지 쉽게 짐작이 가질 않았다.

나는 망설이다 입을 열었다.

“시신은 찾았습니까?”

“아무것도 없었다.”

벌써 몇 달이 흘렀다.

지금까지 혈로(血路)만 걸어온 인생. 시신을 수습해 줄 수하들도 함께 죽었으니 변덕스러운 날씨에 파묻혔거나, 굶주린 짐승들의 먹이가 되었을 것이다.

“늙은이의 욕심이다. 추하고 부질없는.”

쪼르륵.

술잔을 채우는 소리가 유난히 크게 들렸다.

“아까는 취하셨다면서요?”

“영악한 놈. 다 알면서 묻기는.”

전각 안을 환하게 메운 촛불이 그의 인영을 비춘다.

피식, 소리 내어 웃음을 흘린 적천강이 술잔을 꺾었다.

“크. 좋다.”

한 잔 술에 시름을 털어 버린 듯 후련한 목소리다.

문득 적천강이 조필이 죽은 자리를 찾아간 것은, 아직 그를 붙잡고 있는 후회와 미련을 떨쳐 내기 위해서였을 거라는 생각이 들었다.

나는 애써 밝은 목소리로 말했다.

“좋은 건 나눠야 한다고 배웠습니다만.”

“난 어릴 때부터 남의 것을 탐하는 놈은 화염신장으로 지져 버려야 한다고 배웠다.”

“어느 무시무시한 분이 그런 말을 했습니까?”

“내 스승님.”

역시 볼케이노문이야. 가차 없지.

어떤 놈이건 간에 화염신장으로 죄다 지져 버리는구나.

열화문의 역사와 역대 문주가 누구인지는 모르지만 적천강을 보고 있자면 얼추 짐작이 간다.

‘역사 깊은 깡패 문파.’

콩 심은 데 콩 나고 팥 심은 데 팥 난다고 했다.

그 스승에 그 제자지 뭐. 물론 조필의 경우는 예외지만.

‘그나저나 이런 얘기를 하러 온 게 아닌데.’

말없이 술만 홀짝거리는 인영을 바라보며 눈치를 살피던 그때. 적천강이 불쑥 입을 열었다.

“앞으로 화천검(火天劍)은 네 것이다.”

“화, 뭐요?”

“화천검. 네 녀석에게 맡긴 검 말이다.”

[이름 없는 검]의 진짜 이름을 알게 됐지만 지금 그게 문제가 아니다. 나는 놀라서 말까지 더듬었다.

“하, 하지만 이건 열화문의 신물이잖아요.”

“아, 신물.”

몇 잔째인지 모를 술잔을 기울인 적천강이 말을 이었다.

“그거 거짓말이다.”

“예?”

“신물 아니라고. 백 년 전쯤인가, 본문의 문주였던 어느 분이 쓰시던 걸 후대가 물려받은 거지. 오래되긴 했지만 뭐, 당시에도 신병이기(神兵利器)라 불릴 정도였으니 아직 쓸 만할 게다.”

“……!”

아니, 이게 무슨 개소리야.

나는 생각지도 못한 충격적인 진실에 입을 딱 벌렸다.

“그게 다 거짓말이었다고요? 지금 저 놀리시는 거죠?”

“놀려? 너 같은 핏덩이를 뭣 하러?”

“사람들 앞에서 그러셨잖아요! 저놈에게 열화문의 신물을 맡겼다!”

“그랬지. 사람들 앞이니까.”

적천강이 심드렁한 목소리로 말을 이었다.

“그 정도는 해 줘야 세인들이 떠들 것 아니냐. 아, 저놈이 화왕과 깊은 연관이 있구나. 신물을 맡겼으니 제자가 아닐까. 태원진가를 건드리면 그 무시무시한 화왕이 나서겠구나. 뭐 그런 소문이 일파만파 퍼지겠지.”

“…….”

“설마 노부가 네 녀석 같은 애송이한테 본문의 신물을 맡기겠느냐? 어차피 일인전승이라 아는 사람도 없는데 내가 신물이라고 하면 그게 신물인 거지.”

“…….”

“그러니 검은 계속 갖고 있어라. 그래야 종남파 놈들이 감히 나서지 못할 테니.”

이거 꿈인가. 충격에 빠진 내 귓가로 확인 사살을 알리는 시스템 알림이 울렸다.

띠링.

갱신된 정보는 적천강의 말 그대로였다. 십 대 문주가 사용하던 애검. 열화문의 신물이라는 말은 눈 씻고 찾아봐도 없다.

그나마 검에 숨겨져 있다는 ‘진정한 힘’조차도 열화문의 진전을 이어야 한단다.

한마디로 만년한철인 것을 빼면 시체라는 뜻.

‘난 진짜 신물인 줄 알았는데. 열화문의 제자로 삼겠다고 하면 어쩌나 엄청 고민했는데…….’

허탈하게 홀로그램 창을 바라보는 내게 적천강이 선심 쓰는 듯 덧붙였다.

“장기 대여라고 생각해라. 노부가 깜빡하고 그대로 죽어 버리면 가져도 좋다. 아, 화염신장의 비급은 지금 당장 뱉어 내고.”

“망할 늙은이…… 헉.”

생각만 한다는 게 그만 입 밖으로 튀어나와 버렸다.

화들짝 놀라 입을 다문 그 순간, 굳게 닫혀 있던 전각의 문이 그대로 터져 나갔다.

우지직!

화염이 이글거리는 한 쌍의 눈동자가 날 응시했다.

“이 핏덩이 같은 놈이. 방금 뭐라 했느냐?”

“마, 마, 말실수였는데요.”

“말실수? 그럼 노부도 손 실수 한 번 하마.”

후욱!

붉게 달아오른 손바닥과 압도적인 열기.

나는 뒤도 돌아보지 않고 몸을 돌렸다. 찰나의 순간 인벤토리에서 꺼낸 화염신장의 비급을 던지는 것도 잊지 않았다.

“헉, 비급, 화염신장의 비급이!”

그대로 손을 뻗었다가는 비급이 잿가루가 될 판.

대경한 적천강이 황급히 주먹을 거둬들인다. 나는 그 틈을 타 죽을힘을 다해 뛰었다.

“죄송합니다! 진짜 죄송해요! 살려 주세요!”

“이, 이 죽일 놈! 거기 안 서!”

등 뒤로 그의 고함이 쩌렁쩌렁 울렸다.



* * *



꽁지가 빠지도록 도망가는 진태경의 뒷모습을 바라보던 적천강이 피식 웃었다.

방금 전까지 얼굴에 가득하던 분노의 기색은 씻은 듯이 사라진 후였다.

“이놈아, 네가 아무리 도망쳐 봐야 노부의 손바닥 안이니라.”

잡으려 한다면 얼마든지 잡을 수 있다.

그러나 적천강은 뒷짐을 지고 돌아섰다.

자식처럼 아끼던 제자, 장천을 죽인 장본인이지만 진태경에 대한 증오는 없다. 오히려 적천강이 진심으로 사과해야 할 사람 중 하나다.

이 모든 것은 십 년 전, 그의 잘못된 선택으로부터 비롯되었으니까.

“망할 늙은이라고 했지.”

핏덩이 같은 어린놈에게 폭언을 들었음에도 기분이 나쁘지 않았다. 아니, 오히려 후련하기까지 했다.

“그렇지. 나야 말로 망할 늙은이고 노망난 늙은이지. 허허, 허허허.”

스승이 죽은 이후, 감히 어느 누구도 적천강의 면전에서 그를 비난하거나 욕하지 못했다.

그는 화왕이니까. 홀로 전설을 써 내려간 위대한 무인이니까.

그러던 차에 진태경의 한마디를 들으니 오랫동안 막혀 있던 뭔가가 뻥 뚫린 기분이다.

“시원하군. 시원해.”

하루하루 늙어 갈수록 사람은 외로워진다. 살을 맞댈 존재가 없어서가 아니라, 마음을 기댈 존재가 없기 때문이다.

누군가의 버팀목이 될 수는 있지만 누군가에게 기대기에는 너무 늙어 버렸다.

“누군가의 버팀목이라…….”

적천강은 거칠고 날카로운 가시나무였다. 살아온 세월이 있는지라 실로 많은 사람들을 스쳐 갔지만, 그는 그 누구에게도 자신에게 기대는 것을 허락하지 않았다.

그러나 단 한 사람, 장천은 예외였다.

“너는 어떠했느냐? 한순간이라도 이 스승이 든든한 버팀목으로 느껴졌더냐?”

그를 떠올린 적천강의 눈빛이 흐릿해졌다. 그러나 이제는 전만큼 가슴이 아프지도, 눈이 뜨거워지지도 않았다.

죽은 이는 이미 한 줌 흙으로 돌아갔다.

적천강은 제자가 피를 뿌리며 쓰러졌을 그 어딘가에서 한 병의 술을 마시고 한 동이의 술을 뿌렸다.

지난 십 년간 흘리지 못한 눈물을 펑펑 흘리며 마음의 한 또한 함께 흘려보냈다.

“미안하구나. 널 생각하는 것은 오늘이 마지막이다.”

다음이 있다면 그것은 내세(來世)의 일.

문득문득 죽은 제자를 떠올릴 때가 있을지도 모른다. 그러나 그것은 지난날에 대한 후회가 아닌 추억일 것이다.

“이걸로 됐다. 이러면 되는 게야.”

한참 동안 마당을 서성이던 적천강이 멈칫했다. 눈앞에 어른거리던 장천의 얼굴이 사라지고 생각지도 못한 놈이 떠올랐기 때문이었다.

‘이놈이 왜?’

시원시원하게 생긴 이목구비. 자신만만하면서도 어딘지 모르게 밉살맞은 웃음.

그리고 눈치를 살살 살피면서도 그의 날 선 말들을 받아 주는 모습까지.

‘아까 망할 늙은이라고 한 것 때문에 나도 모르게 화가 났나?’

적천강이 미간을 찌푸리던 그때였다.

치지직.

뭔가가 타들어 가는 소리와 함께 가느다란 연기가 피어올랐다.

소리의 진원지를 알아챈 그가 눈을 부릅떴다.

“비, 비급!”

이미 겉장이 반쯤 타 버린 화염신장의 비급을 본 적천강이 노호성을 내질렀다.

“진태경! 이 쳐 죽일 놈아-!”

By embracing the Mount Heng Sword Sect, Jin Wikyung had made a bold move that won the loyalty of dozens of small and mid-sized sects. The Zhongnan Sect’s intervention and the appearance of Fire King Jeok Cheongang, whom everyone had believed dead, had left them all stunned.

Crack!

“Gasp! The manual! The Flame Divine Palm manual!”

“I’m sorry! I’m really sorry! Please spare me!”

“You damned bastard! Stop right there!”

His roar thundered behind me.

The anger that had filled his face only moments ago had vanished without a trace.

Everything had begun with the wrong choice Jeok Cheongang had made ten years ago.

“That’s right. I am a damn old man. A senile old man, too. Heh heh. Heh heh heh.”

After his Master died, no one had dared criticize or curse Jeok Cheongang to his face.

He was the Fire King, a great martial artist who had single-handedly written himself into legend.

Jeok Cheongang could serve as someone else’s support, but he had grown too old to lean on anyone himself.

“To be someone’s support…”

There had been only one exception.

Jangcheon.

“What about you? Did you ever feel, even for a moment, that this Master was a dependable support?”

The dead had already returned to a handful of earth.

At the place where his Disciple had fallen in a spray of blood, Jeok Cheongang had drunk a bottle of liquor and poured out an entire crockful.

He had wept freely, shedding the tears he had been unable to shed for the past ten years and letting the grief in his heart flow out with them.

“I’m sorry. Today will be the last time I think of you.”

If there was to be a next time, it would be in the next life.

The image of Jangcheon that had been flickering before his eyes vanished, replaced by someone he had never expected to think of.

*Why him?*

Open, well-defined features. A confident smile that somehow managed to be irritating.

The way he cautiously gauged Jeok Cheongang’s mood, yet still took every cutting remark in stride.

*Did I get angry without realizing it because he called me a damn old man?*

Sizzle.

“The manual!”

The cover of the Flame Divine Palm manual was already half-burned.

Jeok Cheongang let out a furious roar.

“Jin Taekyung! You damned bastard!”

Jeok Cheongang let out a furious roar.

“Jin Taekyung! You damned bastard!”

Calling the banquet held on New Year’s Day a resounding success still felt like an understatement.

By embracing the Mount Heng Sword Sect, Jin Wikyung had made a bold move that won the loyalty of dozens of small and mid-sized sects. The Zhongnan Sect’s intervention and the appearance of Fire King Jeok Cheongang, whom everyone had believed dead, had left them all stunned.

And…

*I was one of them.*

I ate, drank, and moved from place to place. Wherever I went, people’s eyes followed my every move.

Half a day ago, those gazes had meant interest in the Sleeping Dragon of Shanxi.

Not anymore.

*The Fire King’s Disciple. The heir to the Fire Gate Clan.*

I heard those words everywhere. People talked endlessly about what it meant that Jeok Cheongang, the current Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan, had entrusted me with the sect’s sacred treasure—and why he had protected the Jin Family of Taiyuan even at the cost of making an enemy of the Zhongnan Sect.

*This already seems to be half-confirmed as fact.*

To be honest, I didn’t understand Jeok Cheongang’s intentions either.

That was why I was here.

Everyone was still distracted, and I had managed to slip away unnoticed. This was my chance.

“Phew.”

I took a deep breath.

I stood before the pavilion where Jeok Cheongang had been given lodging. Someone must have ordered everyone to stay away, because there wasn’t so much as a mouse near the large building.

“Great Hero Jeok. Are you there?”

A reply came from beyond the door.

“I’m sleeping.”

“I came because there’s something I wanted to ask you.”

“I said I’m sleeping.”

“…How are you answering me if you’re asleep?”

“I’m sleepwalking.”

Was that an answer or a whinny?

It made no sense, but if the Fire King said that was how it was, then that was how it was. I pulled myself together and tried again.

“Um, there’s something I can’t stop wondering about.”

“Is this old man responsible for satisfying your curiosity?”

“No, but…”

“If you know that, go wash your feet and get some sleep.”

Talk about an impenetrable defense.

But I couldn’t back down now.

I began creeping ever so carefully toward the firmly closed door.

“Take one more step, and you won’t live to see tomorrow’s sunrise.”

“…How did you know?”

“To this old man, your presence is no different from a clap of thunder.”

“Come on. Couldn’t you let me in now? It’s still winter, and it’s rather chilly out here.”

“Would you like this old man to warm you up with the Flame Divine Palm?”

“…”

Just hearing that made my insides feel warm.

When I shut my mouth, silence fell. After a while, Jeok Cheongang broke it with a single sentence.

“I went to Jeongyang.”

“Ah.”

Even an insignificant bead could hold special meaning for someone. Jeongyang was like that.

Jeongyang was merely one of the dozens of counties and towns in Shanxi Province, but Jeok Cheongang had a reason to visit a mountain path there.

*Jopil.*

On the day snow came pouring from the sky, a man who had lived as Jangcheon died under the name Jopil.

“I stayed for a long time at the place you told me about. Some passersby saw an old man wandering around the foot of the mountain and asked why I was there.”

His subdued voice continued.

“I told them that a blood relative had died right there. That I had come because I wanted to recover whatever remained of his body.”

“…”

“That was when I realized something. Even if I had met that boy before you did, I could never have killed him. I would have let him go again, only to regret it afterward.”

It was difficult to imagine what expression Jeok Cheongang wore on the other side of the door.

After hesitating, I asked, “Did you find his body?”

“Nothing was left.”

Several months had already passed.

Jopil had spent his entire life walking a path of blood. The subordinates who might have recovered his body had died alongside him, so whatever remained had likely been buried by the capricious weather or devoured by hungry beasts.

“It is nothing but an old man’s selfish desire. Ugly and futile.”

Glug.

The sound of liquor filling a cup seemed unusually loud.

“I thought you said you were drunk earlier.”

“You crafty brat. Why ask when you already know?”

The candlelight flooding the pavilion outlined his silhouette.

Jeok Cheongang let out a quiet laugh, then tossed back his drink.

“Ahh. Good.”

His voice sounded refreshed, as though that one cup had washed away his troubles.

It occurred to me that Jeok Cheongang had gone to the place where Jopil died to free himself from the regret and lingering attachment that still held him.

I deliberately brightened my voice.

“I was taught that good things should be shared.”

“I was taught from a young age that anyone who coveted what belonged to others should be burned with the Flame Divine Palm.”

“What terrifying person taught you that?”

“My Master.”

That was the Volcano Gate Clan for you. Ruthless.

They burned everyone with the Flame Divine Palm, no matter who it was.

I didn’t know the history of the Fire Gate Clan or the names of its past Sect Leaders, but looking at Jeok Cheongang, I could make a rough guess.

*An old sect of thugs.*

They said beans grew where beans were planted and red beans where red beans were planted.

Like master, like disciple. Jopil was the exception, of course.

*Anyway, this isn’t what I came here to talk about.*

I was watching the silhouette inside the pavilion while trying to read the situation when Jeok Cheongang suddenly spoke.

“From now on, the Fire Heaven Sword is yours.”

“Fire… what?”

“The Fire Heaven Sword. The sword I entrusted to you.”

I had just learned the Unnamed Sword’s true name, but that wasn’t the issue right now. I was so shocked that I stammered.

“B-but that’s the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure.”

“Ah, the sacred treasure.”

Jeok Cheongang tipped back yet another cup of liquor before continuing.

“That was a lie.”

“What?”

“It isn’t a sacred treasure. One of our sect’s Sect Leaders used it about a hundred years ago, and later generations inherited it from him. It’s old, but it was already renowned as a divine weapon back then, so it should still be useful.”

“…!”

What the hell was he talking about?

I stood there with my mouth hanging open at this shocking truth I had never expected.

“That was all a lie? You’re messing with me, right?”

“Messing with you? Why would I bother with a little pup like you?”

“You said it in front of everyone! ‘I entrusted that boy with the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure!’”

“I did. Because we were in front of everyone.”

Jeok Cheongang continued in an indifferent voice.

“I had to go that far to get people talking. ‘That boy must have a deep connection to the Fire King. Perhaps he is the Fire King’s Disciple, since he was entrusted with the sacred treasure. If anyone touches the Jin Family of Taiyuan, that terrifying Fire King will step in.’ Rumors like that will spread far and wide.”

“…”

“Do you really think this old man would entrust our sect’s sacred treasure to a young brat like you? Our arts are passed down to only one successor per generation, so no one else knows the truth. If I say it is a sacred treasure, then it is a sacred treasure.”

“…”

“So keep the sword. That way, those Zhongnan bastards won’t dare make a move.”

*Is this a dream?*

As I stood there in shock, a System notification rang in my ears, delivering the final blow.

Ding.

>

> **Fire Heaven Sword**

> **Grade:** Peak

After passing through the hands of countless owners over many years, it changed of its own accord. Only one who has inherited the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy can draw out its true power.
>
> **Effect:** Unknown

The updated information was exactly as Jeok Cheongang had said.

It was the beloved sword of the tenth Sect Leader. No matter how hard I looked, there wasn’t a single mention of it being the Fire Gate Clan’s sacred treasure.

Even the “true power” hidden within the sword could only be drawn out by someone who had inherited the Fire Gate Clan’s legacy.

In other words, other than the fact that it was made of Ten-Thousand-Year Cold Iron, the sword was a corpse.

*I really thought it was a sacred treasure. I spent so much time worrying about what I’d do if he said he wanted to make me his Disciple…*

As I stared blankly at the holographic window, Jeok Cheongang added as though he were doing me a great favor.

“Think of it as a long-term loan. If this old man forgets about it and dies, you may keep it. Ah, and hand over the Flame Divine Palm manual right now.”

“Damn old man… Gasp.”

I had only meant to think it, but the words slipped out of my mouth.

I clapped my mouth shut in alarm. At that very moment, the firmly closed pavilion door burst outward.

Crack!

A pair of eyes blazing with fire glared at me.

“You little pup. What did you just say?”

“I-I-I misspoke.”

“Misspoke? Then this old man will make a little mistake with his hand, too.”

Whoosh!

A palm glowed red-hot, radiating overwhelming heat.

I spun around without looking back. In the same instant, I pulled the Flame Divine Palm manual from my Inventory and threw it.

“Gasp! The manual! The Flame Divine Palm manual!”

If he reached out now, the manual would turn to ash.

Jeok Cheongang, startled, hastily pulled back his fist. I took advantage of the opening and ran with all my might.

“I’m sorry! I’m really sorry! Please spare me!”

“You damned bastard! Stop right there!”

His roar thundered behind me.

* * *

Jeok Cheongang watched Jin Taekyung flee as though his tail were on fire and let out a quiet laugh.

The anger that had filled his face only moments ago had vanished without a trace.

“You little fool. No matter how far you run, you are still in the palm of this old man’s hand.”

He could catch Taekyung whenever he wished.

But Jeok Cheongang merely clasped his hands behind his back and turned away.

Jin Taekyung had killed Jangcheon, the Disciple Jeok Cheongang had cherished like a son.

Yet Jeok Cheongang bore him no hatred.

If anything, Taekyung was one of the people to whom Jeok Cheongang owed a sincere apology.

Everything had begun with the wrong choice Jeok Cheongang had made ten years ago.

“He called me a damn old man.”

Despite being cursed by a little pup, Jeok Cheongang wasn’t offended.

No, if anything, he felt relieved.

“That’s right. I am a damn old man. A senile old man, too. Heh heh. Heh heh heh.”

After his Master died, no one had dared criticize or curse Jeok Cheongang to his face.

He was the Fire King, a great martial artist who had single-handedly written himself into legend.

And yet, hearing that one remark from Jin Taekyung made him feel as though something that had been blocked for a long time had suddenly burst open.

“How refreshing. Truly refreshing.”

As people grow older, they become lonelier day by day. Not because they have no one with whom to share their warmth, but because they have no one to lean on.

Jeok Cheongang could serve as someone else’s support, but he had grown too old to lean on anyone himself.

“To be someone’s support…”

Jeok Cheongang was a rough, sharp thorn tree. He had lived a long life and crossed paths with countless people, but he had never allowed anyone to lean on him.

There had been only one exception.

Jangcheon.

“What about you? Did you ever feel, even for a moment, that this Master was a dependable support?”

As Jeok Cheongang thought of him, his gaze clouded over. But his chest no longer hurt as much as it once had, nor did his eyes grow hot.

The dead had already returned to a handful of earth.

At the place where his Disciple had fallen in a spray of blood, Jeok Cheongang had drunk a bottle of liquor and poured out an entire crockful.

He had wept freely, shedding the tears he had been unable to shed for the past ten years and letting the grief in his heart flow out with them.

“I’m sorry. Today will be the last time I think of you.”

If there was to be a next time, it would be in the next life.

He might still think of his dead Disciple from time to time. But those thoughts would no longer be regrets about the past.

They would be memories.

“This is enough. This is how it should be.”

After pacing around the courtyard for a long while, Jeok Cheongang suddenly stopped.

The image of Jangcheon that had been flickering before his eyes vanished, replaced by someone he had never expected to think of.

*Why him?*

Open, well-defined features. A confident smile that somehow managed to be irritating.

The way he cautiously gauged Jeok Cheongang’s mood, yet still took every cutting remark in stride.

*Did I get angry without realizing it because he called me a damn old man?*

Jeok Cheongang was frowning when—

Sizzle.

The sound of something burning filled the air, followed by a thin trail of smoke.

Realizing where the sound had come from, his eyes flew open.

“Th-the manual!”

The cover of the Flame Divine Palm manual was already half-burned.

Jeok Cheongang let out a furious roar.

“Jin Taekyung! You damned bastard!”
